inv:A1.0: At the cusp, the natural map $H^1(W;\mathbb C)\to H^1(W,\mathcal O_W)$ is an isomorphism. In degree two the comparison is surjective and is injective on $\ker[H^2(W;\mathbb C)\to H^2(\mathrm{dP}_6;\mathbb C)]$. The cup product $\bigwedge^2H^1(W,\mathcal O_W)\to H^2(W,\mathcal O_W)$ is an isomorphism. Every base-change map $(R^qf_*\mathcal O_X)\otimes k(b)\to H^q(X_b,\mathcal O_{X_b})$ is an isomorphism, including at the nonreduced fibres.
inv:C3.1: Restriction $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)\to H^1(X_b,\mathcal O_{X_b})$ is injective for every scheme-theoretic fibre; on a smooth fibre its image is $\mathbb C\gamma^{0,1}$.
inv:C3.3: For $h=1$, the nine classes specified in \eqref{wb:eq:bcpr-generators}, together with the unit, give bases of every nonzero Bott--Chern group.
